clue.text: Not appropriate to a person in care

blocks.note: unto is an old word for to
a ward is someone placed in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: Something is judged unsuitable to say or do to somebody being looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward behaviour is improper or unseemly, the opposite of what is fitting.

clue.text: Report circulating -- extraterrestrial landed on Scottish isle

indicators.note: in a down clue, landed on puts the first thing above the second
circulating turns things round, so the whole run is read backwards

blocks.note: ET is the film alien, short for extraterrestrial
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A rumour goes round that an alien has touched down on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give a spoken or written account of events, much as one reports them.

clue.text: Improving other people in upright surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings are what encircle something, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: first part of on end, meaning upright
them refers to other people, as opposed to us
second part of on end, meaning upright

explanation.surface: Someone's condition gets better among others who are respectable and upstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the mend is recovering from illness or injury, getting better day by day.

clue.text: Current in a widened stretch of river

blocks.note: taken as written
the Norfolk Broads are lakes formed by widened rivers

explanation.surface: A flow of water moving through a wider section of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' wants to be a river's flow; it is the adjective, as in a rumour is abroad. The Broads are a waterway region in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that is abroad is circulating widely, in general currency among people.

clue.text: Make every effort to excel, following Carver's elevation

indicators.note: following says the word before it is placed after what comes next

blocks.note: Carver Doone is the villain of the novel Lorna Doone
a level is a height or elevation
to best is to outdo or excel

explanation.surface: Try hard to succeed, following the high standard set by a woodcarver.
explanation.walkthrough: Carver looks like a craftsman, but it is Carver Doone, the brutal outlaw in R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's level best is an idiom for trying as hard as one possibly can.

clue.text: Packing in sport

blocks.note: first meaning: putting things into crates or cartons
second meaning: fighting with gloved fists in a ring

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting kit ready for a game; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both enclosing goods in cartons and the fist-fighting contest held in a ring.

clue.text: Fairground ride is not a weighable contraption

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the following letter out
a contraption is something cobbled together, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: the letter to remove
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A funfair attraction is said to be a machine too big to put on scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A big wheel is the tall revolving passenger wheel at a funfair, also called a Ferris wheel.

clue.text: Take off from Italian capital, and marry outside Italy

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter
outside means the word before wraps around the word after

blocks.note: the first letter of Italian
to mate is to pair up or marry
IT is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: A plane departs from Rome, and someone weds abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests a plane leaving the airport; here it means mimicry, as an impressionist takes off a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or impersonate them, copying their manner for comic effect.

clue.text: Celebrity estranges constituents

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the word is broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A famous politician alienates the voters in their district.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity in the sense of fame or renown is close to greatness, eminence and distinction.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment worthy of more note, they say

indicators.note: they say points to how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: something worthy of more note is more great

explanation.surface: Someone praises a kitchen gadget as deserving more attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a utensil with sharp-edged holes for shredding cheese or vegetables in cooking.

clue.text: Ignores a dubious order

definitions.note: a verb here: to put in order

indicators.note: something dubious is not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone disregards an instruction they think questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like the noun being ignored, but it is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise something is to arrange it systematically, putting its parts into proper sequence.

clue.text: Beat and scold angrily, resulting in distress

blocks.note: to lace someone is an old word for to thrash them
to rate is to berate or rebuke harshly

explanation.surface: Physical and verbal punishment leaves someone upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides tearing flesh, lacerate can mean wounding someone's feelings, causing them great pain.

clue.text: Pub in tropical capital

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: the tropics are hot
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A drinking spot in some steamy equatorial city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tropical capital' reads as one phrase, but tropical is only the outer wordplay; Hobart is in cool Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of the Australian state of Tasmania.

clue.text: Party in the back bar

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following word from its end to its start

blocks.note: a lever is a bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: A celebration held in the rear room of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back bar' sounds like a part of a pub; bar is a lever, written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively, noisy celebration, much like a party with drinking and dancing.

clue.text: Arcane ritual gripping subordinate after the head has gone

indicators.note: with its head gone a word loses its opening letter
gripping means holding on all sides, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a rite is a ritual
a second is an assistant or deputy

explanation.surface: A mysterious ceremony seizes an underling once the leader has departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recondite is obscure and little known, requiring specialist knowledge to grasp.

clue.text: Patrons find second bit of decay in horizontal beams in church

indicators.note: second bit of asks for just the letter in position two of the word
find something in a place means it sits inside it
in puts everything before it inside the church abbreviation

blocks.note: first half of CE, the Church of England
a lintel is the horizontal beam over a door or window
the second letter of decay
second half of CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: Churchgoers spot rot in the timber crossbeams of their church.
explanation.walkthrough: The E goes inside LINTEL, and the result inside CE (Church of England). The clue's plural beams stands for the singular lintel.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers or patrons who regularly use a business.

clue.text: One who treats the criminal

blocks.note: taken as written
a type of violent criminal

explanation.surface: Someone offers treatment to an offender.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a prison counsellor; the answer simply splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist gives remedial treatment for mental or physical disorders.

clue.text: Sign of contempt about a smug circular

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encircles the others

blocks.note: scorn is contempt
pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious or smug
the letter O is circular

explanation.surface: Someone shows disdain for a self-satisfied leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi is British slang for pious. PIO goes inside SCORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the scorpion, is the eighth sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Leading Conservative unfortunately unvoiced

definitions.note: conducive is always followed by to: leading (to)

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A senior Tory politician sadly could not get their views heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading Conservative' reads as a party grandee; leading is the definition and Conservative only gives C, which joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conducive to a result tends to bring it about, just as a road leads somewhere.

clue.text: Garment said to be worth a few pounds

indicators.note: said points to how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: knickers are women's underpants; the K is silent

explanation.surface: An item of clothing is reckoned to cost a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: A nicker is British slang for a pound sterling, and its plural can be nicker or nickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicker is old London slang for one pound, so several of them make a few pounds.

clue.text: Ultimately many have a violent animus, for this poet

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so we take the closing letter of each word

blocks.note: the final letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Plenty of people end up with fierce hostility toward a particular poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the great Irish poet, author of The Second Coming and Sailing to Byzantium.

clue.text: One has to accept an upset in the wake of an earthquake

definitions.text: in the wake of an earthquake
definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: what comes after an earthquake

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside
in a down clue, upset turns the whole thing upside down

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
has to means must, an obligation
taken as written

explanation.surface: People must tolerate chaos after a quake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, upset means read upwards. The definition is a looser descriptive phrase: the thing that follows an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, typically set off by an undersea earthquake shortly before it.

clue.text: Count more dead

blocks.note: first meaning: a total or figure
second meaning: having less feeling, said NUM-er

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rising death toll; the second sense is the comparative of numb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a figure arrived at by counting and the comparative of numb, meaning deader to sensation.

clue.text: Delicious drink lying around in locker at Central Station

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
something lying around is turned about, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of locker, all of at and the start of Central
surface padding completing the railway station picture

explanation.surface: A tasty bottle has been left in a station left-luggage locker.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, so the word is used for any delicious beverage.

clue.text: Praise a book the Opium Eater would have liked

definitions.text: the Opium Eater would have liked
definitions.note: a description standing for a noun: what he would have liked

blocks.note: to laud is to praise
taken as written
Num. is the abbreviation for Numbers, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone admires a book that the opium addict author would have enjoyed reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The Opium Eater is Thomas De Quincey, author of Confessions of an English Opium-Eater; the book here is not literature but a Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum is a tincture of opium in alcohol, the drug to which De Quincey was famously addicted.

clue.text: One type of wood is extremely effective for a pedestal

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a verb: to put on a pedestal

indicators.note: extremely points to a letter at an extreme end of the next word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
deal is pine or fir timber
taken as written
an end letter of effective

explanation.surface: A particular timber works very well for making a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is softwood timber. The definition is a cryptic hint: to idealise someone is to put them on a pedestal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealising a person means regarding them as perfect, which the idiom calls placing them on a pedestal.

clue.text: Ribald disruption of wedding

indicators.note: a disruption throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Crude jokes spoil a marriage ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal is the adjective for things belonging to a bride or a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Flag officer

blocks.note: first meaning: a banner flown by a ship
second meaning: a junior commissioned officer, especially in the US Navy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officer' is a real naval rank (an admiral), which hides that the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a naval banner and a low-ranking commissioned officer, once the standard-bearer.

clue.text: Having shot dog, beat it

blocks.note: a shot at something is a go or turn
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: After firing at a dog, somebody runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'dog' look like a verb and its victim; they are both nouns-turned-synonyms, and 'beat it' is slang for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to flee, just as the slang command beat it means go away fast.
